subject: Capacity thresholds and QoS envelope for Acme VPC GPU pool
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity envelope proposal for Acme VPC GPU pool

Team,

Following last week's architecture review with Acme, I've sketched an initial capacity envelope we should present in tomorrow's joint call. Key asks from Acme: low single-digit tail latency for interactive workflows, predictable per-month token spend, and strict egress caps inside their VPC. We need a conservative-but-actionable starting point that trades cost for predictable headroom.

High-level assumptions (please sanity-check):
- Baseline model flavor: open-llama-70B-ish => baseline 1.8k tokens/sec per H100 (serving decoder-only, beam=1).
- Target sustained throughput (customer): 120k tokens/sec sustained, 300k tokens/sec burst for 10-minute windows.
- Concurrency shape: 95th percentile spikes up to 1,100 concurrent sessions, median concurrent 420.
- Cache hit assumption: 20% prefix/KV-cache hit for steady-state; warm-up needs accounted.
- Network egress budget: 80 MB/s sustained across the VPC (egress throttled at their subnet).

Initial sizing sketch (rough):
- Primary pool: 16 H100 nodes (8 GPUs/node assumed for on-prem nodal config) => logical GPU count 128.
- Expected nominal aggregate tokens/sec (no caching): 128 * 1.8k = 230k tps. With 20% cache hits => ~184k effective tps.
- Headroom margin: recommend 1.4x comfortable headroom over customer target => supports sustained 120k and burst 300k within burst window via warm pool and admission control.

Operational controls we should commit to in the doc:
1) QoS classes (gold/silver/bronze) with explicit admission thresholds and pre-warm policies.
2) Token-level throttles and circuit breakers (per-customer/route) with explicit SLOs and fallback variants.
3) Network shaping mapping per-class to ensure egress budgets aren't violated.
4) Warm-pool sizing and warmup probes (periodic synthetic traffic to maintain KV cache TTLs).

I've attached a first-pass capacity model (acme_capacity_model_v1.xlsx) and a diagram for the VPC QoS topology. Jonas, can you verify per-GPU tps and the headroom multiplier? Karthik, can you validate the concurrency shape assumptions against our traffic model generator? Marissa/Grace, any concerns on the ops/playbook side (SRE runbooks, probe cadence)?

Thanks,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity envelope proposal for Acme VPC GPU pool

Hannah — thanks for the clear outline. Quick checks and adjustments to numbers below after a short sim run: 

1) Per-GPU throughput: our H100 macrobench (seq_len=1024, sampling) pegs at ~1.6k–1.9k tps depending on tokenizer and KV locality. 1.8k is a reasonable central estimate.

2) Warm-pool behavior: to hit the 300k burst we need a warm pool sized at roughly 18% of total GPUs (to cover cache locality and burst concurrency). For 128 logical GPUs that implies additional ~23 GPUs in a warm state (we can reserve on same nodes via pinned processes).

3) Admission controls: propose the following QoS admission thresholds (based on our sims):
   - Gold: allow until 85% sustained util per-GPU; pre-warm trigger at 70%.
   - Silver: allow until 65% util; pre-warm at 50%.
   - Bronze: best-effort, admission starts to drop at 45% util.

4) Network egress: 80 MB/s seems tight. For worst-case large-output payloads (2k tokens responses ~4MB), a peak of 300k tps would theoretically exceed egress unless we apply compression or bundle streaming. Recommend we add an outbound shape: reserve 60% of egress for gold traffic and enforce per-connection chunked streaming.

I've updated the attached workbook with a per-GPU utilization curve and a separate tab for warm-pool sizing (acme_capacity_model_v1.xlsx). Also added a small topology sketch for in-VPC policing (vpc_qos_topology_diagram.png).

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.cloudops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed capacity envelope & QoS mapping — Acme VPC GPU pool (for review)

Hi Elena / Carlos —

Thanks again for the session this morning. Per our discussion the attached is our proposed starting envelope for the private VPC deployment and the QoS controls we recommend to meet Acme's latency and budget constraints. This is intentionally conservative — designed to give deterministic performance while you ramp.

Key points we want your confirmation on before we lock the plan:
- Target sustained throughput: 120k tokens/sec, with operational burst to 300k tokens/sec for short windows (<= 10 minutes)
- Pool baseline: 128 logical GPUs (16 nodes at 8 GPUs each, H100-class), plus 23 GPUs sized as warm to absorb bursts.
- QoS classes: Gold (interactive clinician flows), Silver (background inference for analytics), Bronze (batch and async jobs).
- Egress shaping: we will enforce per-class egress limits. Your note about third-party connectors that output large artifacts requires we set an outbound cap — suggested 80 MB/s across the VPC, with prioritization for Gold.

Operational commitments from Redwood:
- Per-route SLOs with explicit admission control and circuit breakers.
- Weekly synthetic probe windows to keep KV caches warm for Gold routes.
- A simple escalation path and an ops playbook (draft attached).

Attachments: acme_capacity_model_v1.xlsx (sizing workbook), vpc_qos_topology_diagram.png (policing zones), draft_operational_playbook_v1.pdf (ops steps and runbooks).

Could you confirm the burst window length you anticipate (we used 10 minutes) and whether you expect many >2k-token responses (that affects egress sizing)? If you approve, we'll convert this into a definitive capacity commitment and SOW paragraph.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.cloudops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed capacity envelope & QoS mapping — Acme VPC GPU pool

Hannah — thanks for the clear proposal and the attachments. Quick answers from our side after an ops sync: 

- Burst windows: 10 minutes is our current planning assumption; we may need occasional extended bursts during morning shift (up to 20 minutes) for batch-to-interactive handoffs — possible once per quarter.
- Large responses: most clinical assistant responses are <1k tokens, but report generation (on-demand) can hit 3k–4k tokens. Those are scheduled and can be routed to Bronze/Silver if needed, but sometimes clinicians request ad-hoc long outputs.
- Egress: 80 MB/s should be considered a hard cap. We cannot increase the subnet egress without an internal procurement lead time (2–4 weeks).

Accept the QoS breakdown in principle. Two asks before sign-off:
1) Can Redwood provide a simple token-compression/streaming recommendation to reduce egress for long reports?
2) Can you add an explicit roll-back plan and an hour-by-hour ramp schedule we can include in the SOW?

If you can incorporate those, we can move to the SOW draft stage.

Thanks,
Elena

Elena Ruiz
Head of Cloud Operations, Acme Health

Internal follow-up / action items based on Elena's reply: 

1) Token-compression/egress mitigation: Jonas + Karthik to draft a recommendation for streaming chunk sizes, gzip-level experiment matrix, and a fallback to server-side summarization for >2k token outputs. Deliverable: short doc + perf numbers by Thu EOD.
2) Ramp & rollback schedule: Marissa to author an hour-by-hour 4-step ramp (10%/35%/70%/100%) with explicit rollback triggers (latency P95 > 250ms for Gold, egress > 75 MB/s, >5% error rate over 5 minutes). Deliverable: first draft by Wed noon.
3) SOW paragraph: Hannah to draft the capacity commitment language and include warm-pool sizing and burst guarantees. Draft to Elena for sign-off by Friday.
4) Playbook updates: Grace to add a probe cadence appendix and emergency contact list.

I'll assign the tasks in the project tracker and link to the drive. We'll keep Acme looped for progress updates.

Thanks all — good momentum here.

Hannah
